metadata.document: Reform of the resource management system: The urban context

cleaned_body_text: In its Reform of the Resource Management System project, the Environmental Defence Society has looked, from first principles, at how Aotearoa New Zealand can manage its environment and resources better in the future. A comprehensive rethink is urgently required, not just another round of tinkering to legal frameworks. Over the past three years we have produced two reports on this vast subject. The first analysed the resource management system as a whole and presented options for change. The second report put forward a single preferred model and a timeline for how its pieces could be put into place over a period of years. Towards the end of Phase 2, the government established a panel of experts, ably chaired by the Hon Tony Randerson QC, to investigate resource management system reform and produce independent recommendations. This document marks the conclusion of a third phase of EDS's system reform work, looking specifically at how resource management system change would play out in the urban context. Although the RMA is a key element of the resource management system in and around urban areas, this system is about much more than just that Act. It is about all the formal mechanisms by which we protect and cherish our natural heritage, provide for New Zealanders' social, cultural and economic wellbeing, and preserve resources for future generations. Reform needs to be holistic, synergistic and transformational.
